models.title: Gumbel distribution maximum likelihood estimation
models.description: Uses Newton–Raphson to estimate the parameters of the Gumbel distribution.
models.details: Estimates mu and sigma by centering the data and iterating on sigma; log-likelihood is computed with extraDistr::dgumbel.
references: Johnson, N. L., Kotz, S. and Balakrishnan, N. (1995) Continuous Univariate Distributions, Volume 2, Chapter 22. Wiley, New York.

models.title: Weibull distribution maximum likelihood estimation
models.description: Uses a Gumbel transformation to estimate the Weibull parameters.
models.details: Transforms x via -log(x), calls the Gumbel estimator on the shifted data, and maps back to shape/scale.
references: Johnson, N. L., Kotz, S. and Balakrishnan, N. (1995) Continuous Univariate Distributions, Volume 1, Chapter 21. Wiley, New York.

models.title: Gamma distribution maximum likelihood estimation
models.description: Joint maximum likelihood estimation of Gamma shape and rate.
models.details: Uses Newton–Raphson on log-parameters with method-of-moments starts.
references: Johnson, N. L., Kotz, S. and Balakrishnan, N. (1995) Continuous Univariate Distributions, Volume 1. Wiley, New York.

models.title: Lomax distribution maximum likelihood estimation
models.description: Estimates Lomax (Pareto Type II) parameters via Newton–Raphson on lambda, with kappa in closed form given lambda.
models.details: The Lomax MLE only exists when the data show enough dispersion: specifically `mean(x^2) >= 2 * mean(x)^2` (equivalently, sample CV >= 1). Below that threshold the likelihood has no interior maximum: as `kappa -> Inf` with `lambda * kappa` held constant the Lomax density converges to an Exponential, and the likelihood approaches that limit without ever attaining it. `mllomax()` detects this at entry and stops with a message recommending `mlexp()`. Inputs that satisfy the moment condition are fit by Newton-Raphson on lambda; kappa is then `n / sum(log1p(lambda * x))`.
references: Kleiber, C. and Kotz, S. (2003) Statistical Size Distributions in Economics and Actuarial Sciences. Wiley.

Giles, D. E., Feng, H. and Godwin, R. T. (2013) On the bias of the maximum likelihood estimator for the two-parameter Lomax distribution. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 42(11), 1934-1950.

models.title: Negative Binomial distribution maximum likelihood estimation
models.description: Joint maximum likelihood estimation of size and prob via Newton-Raphson on size.
models.details: The negative binomial MLE only exists when the sample variance exceeds the sample mean (overdispersion). When `var(x) <= mean(x)` the likelihood is maximised in the limit `size -> Inf`, where the negative binomial reduces to a `Poisson(mean)`. `mlnbinom()` detects this case and stops with a message pointing to `mlpois()`.
references: Johnson, N. L., Kotz, S. and Kemp, A. W. (1993) Univariate Discrete Distributions, Chapter 5. Wiley.

models.title: Binomial distribution maximum likelihood estimation
models.description: Joint maximum likelihood estimation of size and prob, optionally with size supplied.
models.details: When `size` is given, `prob = mean(x) / size` in closed form. With size unknown, `mlbinom()` searches over integer sizes from `max(x)` upward and reports the maximiser of the profile likelihood. The estimator does not exist when `var(x) >= mean(x)` (overdispersed data); in that case the likelihood is maximised in the limit `size -> Inf` and `mlbinom()` stops with a message recommending `mlpois()` or that an explicit `size` be supplied.
references: Olkin, I., Petkau, A. J. and Zidek, J. V. (1981) A comparison of n estimators for the binomial distribution. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 76(375), 637-642.
